title: Using AI safely at work
teaser: What to share, and what never to share

basics.say: Last topic, and maybe the most important: using AI safely at work. A simple traffic light helps.
Green: public information and your own drafts with nothing confidential in them – a blog idea, rewording a paragraph, planning your day.
Orange: anything about clients or colleagues. Remove names, emails and figures first, or use a company-approved tool.
Red: never paste passwords, API keys (the secret codes apps use), contracts or confidential client data into an AI tool – not even 'just once'.
And always check the answer before you use it. Your name is on what you send, not the AI's.

deeper.say: Why so careful? Depending on the tool and its settings, what you type may be stored, reviewed or used to improve future models.
Company-approved tools usually come with contracts that protect your data. Personal accounts usually don't.
Watch for hidden instructions too: a web page or document can contain text meant to trick an AI assistant into doing something else.
When in doubt, ask before you paste, and follow your company's AI policy – it beats any rule of thumb I can give you.

takeaway: Share green, anonymize orange, never paste red – and always check the answer.
